requirements.requirement: At least 512MB of compressed in-memory (zram) swap configured
requirements.summary: zram-generator.conf sets zram-size=1024 with compression-algorithm=zstd; zramctl/swapon confirm /dev/zram0 is 1G, zstd-compressed, and active as swap, both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: zram swap active at boot (persistent across restarts)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id and healthy zram state were captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, post-restart boot_id differed confirming an actual restart, and post-restart evidence shows zram0 automatically re-created (systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service exited successfully) with 1G zstd swap active at priority 100 with no manual re-activation step.

requirements.requirement: zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: swap-priority=100 was set for zram0 (high preference), and /etc/fstab and /proc/swaps show no disk-backed swap entries exist to compete, both pre- and post-reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task - at least 512MB of zstd-compressed zram swap, active and preferred at boot - are directly satisfied. The executor also correctly ran the required node-restart evidence protocol on node1: it captured a healthy pre-restart baseline and boot_id, issued and confirmed a reboot acknowledgement, observed a changed boot_id proving the restart occurred, and confirmed zram swap was automatically and correctly re-established afterward without manual intervention. Hygiene is clean with no unnecessary or unresolved mutations.
limitations: Because no disk-backed swap exists on node1, the 'preferred over disk-backed swap' requirement is verified via priority configuration and absence of competing swap rather than a direct head-to-head runtime comparison between zram and disk swap.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace, every state-changing action (installing zram-generator, writing the config file, daemon-reload, starting the zram-setup service, and the final reboot) maps directly to satisfying the task or to the mandated restart-evidence protocol. The transient 'File exists' symlink error during manual generator invocation (cmd-9618759dcfb2457d) was a harmless collision with the generator's own auto-created unit and did not require remediation - the service still started successfully. The only residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small artifact of the reboot command itself, which is low-risk and not the kind of abandoned state that warrants penalty. No disk swap was disabled or altered (none existed), no competing services were left failed, and package-health/listening-socket snapshots show no unwanted changes between before-prepare and after-executor other than the expected boot-id change and ephemeral systemd-private directories tied to the new boot.
